title: 'I Lost My Whole World': Queens Father Seeks Help After Daughter's Death
excerpt: Kuldeep Singh, an Uber driver in Queens, is raising $18,000 for his 5-year-old daughter Fabiana Cabello's funeral after her mother was charged with second-degree murder.
body:
• Fabiana Cabello, 5, was found unresponsive on October 14 at her home in South Richmond Hill, Queens, and was pronounced dead at Jamaica Hospital Medical Center.
  • Her mother, Francis Cabello, 32, was arrested and charged with second-degree murder after allegedly telling a 911 dispatcher, "I killed my daughter."
  • A criminal complaint cited scrapes on the child's face and petechiae in her eyes, heart and lungs, findings associated with asphyxia; the incident window was put at 5:30 p.m. to 6:55 p.m.
  • Father Kuldeep Singh, an Uber driver, is seeking $22,000 through GoFundMe for funeral and cemetery costs, saying losing his daughter feels like losing his whole world.

Five-year-old Fabiana Cabello was found unresponsive at her family home in South Richmond Hill, Queens, on the evening of October 14 and was pronounced dead after being taken to Jamaica Hospital Medical Center. Her mother, Francis Cabello, 32, was arrested and charged with second-degree murder. Her father, Kuldeep Singh, an Indian-origin Uber driver, has since appealed for help to pay for his daughter's funeral.

Police said officers arrived at the home at about 6:55 p.m. following a 911 call. According to reporting cited by The Daily Jagran and The Indian Witness, Cabello allegedly told the dispatcher, "I killed my daughter," and told first responders the child was upstairs and not breathing. Officers found Fabiana unresponsive, with bleeding from her nose.

What the complaint says

A criminal complaint obtained by People placed the incident between 5:30 p.m. and 6:55 p.m. on October 14. It described scrapes on Fabiana's face and petechiae — tiny spots caused by bleeding — in her eyes, heart and lungs. Those findings can be associated with asphyxia, according to the complaint. The official cause of death remains a matter for the medical examiner, and the investigation is continuing.

Cabello was arraigned on October 16. She did not enter a plea at that appearance and was due back in court on October 20, according to the Queens District Attorney's Office as reported in coverage of the case. She was also taken for a psychiatric evaluation. No motive has been publicly established by authorities.

"I loved my daughter very much, and losing her feels like I lost my whole world."

— Kuldeep Singh, on his GoFundMe appeal

A father trying to arrange a funeral

Singh launched a GoFundMe appeal seeking $22,000 to cover funeral and cemetery expenses. In the appeal, he wrote that the funeral home and cemetery were asking for a deposit he could not afford on his own. He said he was trying to keep working as an Uber driver while driving a rental car, but was grieving and struggling to manage the costs at the same time. Coverage of the fundraiser said it had raised $16,780 toward the target by Wednesday.

Singh described Fabiana as a joyful and affectionate child. He recalled that the family often had to remind her not to talk to strangers, and that during a doctor's appointment she hugged the nurses she could see. "Nobody would want to lose her," he told The New York Times, as cited in The Daily Jagran report. "She was such a beautiful child."

Family accounts

Relatives remembered Fabiana as loving and cheerful. Her uncle described how she helped her great-grandmother move around the apartment by holding her hand when her knees hurt, and how she brought happiness to her grandparents. Her grandfather, Franklin Cabello, told reporters the family felt "mentally and physically destroyed" and was placing its confidence in God.

Franklin Cabello also said his daughter had been acting strangely and had stopped taking medication, and that he had been keeping an eye on her. He said he had not expected her to harm the child, describing her as an attentive and protective mother. Those are family accounts reported by outlets including the New York Post; they do not establish why the incident happened, and the case will be tested in court.

What happens next

Cabello remains subject to the criminal process in Queens, with further court proceedings to follow the October 20 date reported earlier. For Singh and the wider family, the immediate task is arranging Fabiana's funeral while the investigation and prosecution continue. Readers who wish to help can donate to the family's fundraiser below.

How to help: Singh's GoFundMe, Funeral Support for My Daughter, covers Fabiana's funeral and cemetery costs and had raised $18,025 toward its $22,000 goal at the time of writing. The campaign is organized by Kuldeep Singh in Jamaica, New York — confirm the organizer's name on the page before donating.
